name: Accessible first
summary: Large text, large targets and AAA contrast, so everyone can finish the task.
description: Accessible first is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Large text, large targets and AAA contrast, so everyone can finish the task.

ai.use_when: Public services, health, government and any product that must work for everyone.
ai.avoid_when: Dense expert tools where screen space matters more than size.

scenarios.text: A person with low vision zooms to 200% and applies for a benefit with a screen magnifier.
A person with a tremor completes a form on a tablet.

summary.text: Plain and direct. Every sentence is easy to read on the first try.

principles.text: Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
One idea per sentence. Put the action first.

inventory.description: The components this system carries, picked from the grammar catalogue by the components answers. Anything not listed is out.

in.why: Every action, with a large target.
Label, hint and error in the same place on every question.
Many choices, each with a large target.
One choice from a short, visible list.
A browser select that every assistive technology understands.
Errors and important notes that stay on the page.
Shows how far through the steps a person is.
Shows where a person is in the service.
Only to confirm leaving with unsaved answers.
Optional help a person can open.
Says that the page is working.

out.why: Hover-only hints fail touch, magnifier and keyboard users.
A custom listbox is harder for screen readers than the native select.
Dragging is hard with a tremor; a text field is exact.
Messages that disappear can be missed; alerts stay.
A checkbox is clearer about what on and off mean.

samples.description: Sample content for showing this system: written from its use scenarios, in its voice, with every status mapped to a meaning. Storybook, the site and the docs read it; it is never shared between schemes.
samples.screen: Apply for support with housing costs

statuses.label: Check your answers
statuses.why: Something needs a second look before you continue.

statuses.label: Upload failed
statuses.why: The file did not reach us and must be sent again.

field.label: Date of birth
field.error: Enter your date of birth. For example, 27 3 1980.

checkbox: Someone is helping me fill in this form

confirm.title: Do you want to cancel your application?

card.title: Step 2 of 4: Your home
card.description: About 3 minutes. You will need your rent agreement.

answers.question: business.q1
answers.why: A public service everyone must be able to use.

answers.question: business.q2
answers.why: One service, one brand.

answers.question: people.q1
answers.why: Everyone, including people with low vision, motor and cognitive needs.

answers.question: people.q2
answers.why: AAA where it applies; nobody is left out.

answers.question: content.q1
answers.why: Most screens are forms and steps.

answers.question: content.q2
answers.why: One question per screen lowers effort.

answers.question: tasks.q1
answers.why: People must finish the form.

answers.question: tasks.q2
answers.why: People do this once or twice a year.

answers.question: human.q1
answers.why: Low effort to understand each step.

answers.question: human.q2
answers.why: Nobody remembers the interface from last time.

answers.question: outcomes.q1
answers.why: Completion without errors is the measure.

answers.question: outcomes.q2
answers.why: A failed form can cost someone a benefit.

answers.question: brand.q1
answers.why: Calm and clear, never clever.

answers.question: brand.q2
answers.why: The brand stays out of the way.

answers.question: scenarios.q1
answers.why: Public services are used on any device, with any assistive technology.

answers.question: scenarios.q2
answers.why: An application is finished in one sitting, or saved and resumed.

answers.question: team.q1
answers.why: A platform team serves many services.

answers.question: team.q2
answers.why: Changes are rare and tested.

answers.question: typography.roles
answers.why: Few roles keep pages predictable.

answers.question: typography.count
answers.why: Only the sizes the screens need, each clearly different.

answers.question: typography.definition
answers.why: Line height grows with text size for zoom users.

answers.question: typography.values
answers.why: Large text is readable for more people.

answers.question: typography.lands
answers.why: Type matters most in form labels and hints.

answers.question: color.roles
answers.why: Few color roles, each with one clear meaning.

answers.question: color.count
answers.why: Primary and secondary only; fewer choices, fewer errors.

answers.question: color.definition
answers.why: True neutrals and one strong blue, checked for contrast.

answers.question: color.values
answers.why: Strong but not loud color.

answers.question: color.lands
answers.why: Links and actions must be found by everyone.

answers.question: spacing.roles
answers.why: Large rows matter for touch and zoom.

answers.question: spacing.count
answers.why: One density; no compact mode to fail people.

answers.question: spacing.definition
answers.why: Big, even steps lower effort.

answers.question: spacing.values
answers.why: Space lowers effort and mis-taps.

answers.question: spacing.lands
answers.why: Space between fields prevents mis-taps.

answers.question: shape.roles
answers.why: Badges keep a clear rectangle.

answers.question: shape.count
answers.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

answers.question: shape.definition
answers.why: One brand, one set of corners.

answers.question: shape.values
answers.why: Clear, slightly rounded controls.

answers.question: shape.lands
answers.why: Corners show on controls and step cards.

answers.question: elevation.roles
answers.why: Flat is easier to read at high zoom.

answers.question: elevation.count
answers.why: No shadows.

answers.question: elevation.definition
answers.why: Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.

answers.question: elevation.values
answers.why: No shadows; borders do the work.

answers.question: elevation.lands
answers.why: Only dialogs separate, with a dimmed page and a border.

answers.question: motion.roles
answers.why: Motion only confirms an action.

answers.question: motion.count
answers.why: One speed.

answers.question: motion.definition
answers.why: A standard ease-out is easy to follow.

answers.question: motion.values
answers.why: Moderate speed is easy to follow.

answers.question: motion.lands
answers.why: Only state changes move.

answers.question: iconography.roles
answers.why: Icons support words; they never replace them.

answers.question: iconography.count
answers.why: One size, larger than the text.

answers.question: iconography.definition
answers.why: Filled icons stay visible at low vision.

answers.question: iconography.values
answers.why: Larger icons are easier to see.

answers.question: iconography.lands
answers.why: Icons work hardest beside status words and errors.

answers.question: theming.roles
answers.why: One brand, so only the mode changes.

answers.question: theming.count
answers.why: Light and dark.

answers.question: theming.definition
answers.why: One service, one brand.

answers.question: theming.values
answers.why: Light and dark ship as standard; both hold AAA text.

answers.question: theming.lands
answers.why: Only colors change.

answers.question: accessibility.roles
answers.why: Every state, including loading, gets its own value.

answers.question: accessibility.count
answers.why: Never color alone.

answers.question: accessibility.definition
answers.why: AAA contrast for text.

answers.question: accessibility.values
answers.why: Large targets for tremor and touch.

answers.question: accessibility.lands
answers.why: Forms are where people are blocked.

answers.question: naming.roles
answers.why: Components get their own keys.

answers.question: naming.count
answers.why: Primitives, semantics and component keys.

answers.question: naming.definition
answers.why: Role names survive a redesign.

answers.question: naming.values
answers.why: Lowercase paths read the same everywhere.

answers.question: naming.lands
answers.why: A component API keeps changes local.

answers.question: voice.roles
answers.why: Hints and help text carry people through each step.

answers.question: voice.count
answers.why: One plain tone everywhere; no surprises.

answers.question: voice.definition
answers.why: A word list of common words, with terms to avoid.

answers.question: voice.values
answers.why: Every sentence is easy to read on the first try.

answers.question: voice.lands
answers.why: Words decide whether a form gets finished.

answers.question: components.roles
answers.why: Forms, steps and feedback are all a public service needs.

answers.question: components.count
answers.why: Only the parts in use, each tested with assistive technology.

answers.question: components.definition
answers.why: A component joins only when it works with any device and assistive technology.

answers.question: components.values
answers.why: One clear way to do each thing.

answers.question: components.lands
answers.why: Components do their work in forms and steps.

usage.why: A clear, consistent title on every page.
Every number must be readable at large size.
Large text and short lines lower effort.

usage.use: type.label, above the field, always visible
usage.why: Labels must stay visible while typing.
Selection never relies on color alone.

usage.use: color.status.danger, an icon and a sentence next to the field
usage.why: People must know what went wrong and where.
Underline works without color perception.

usage.use: Badge with an icon and a word
usage.why: Status must survive no color and a screen reader.
Generous space lowers mis-taps.
Space is easy to see; thin lines are not.
Large rows are easy to read and tap.
Clear rectangles read as fields and buttons.
Clear shapes with a word inside.
Shadows are hard to see; borders are not.

usage.use: A strong border and a dimmed page
usage.why: The dimmed page makes the dialog obvious.
Moderate speed is easy to follow.
When people ask for less motion, nothing moves.

usage.use: Not used: always add a word
usage.why: Icons alone are guesswork.

usage.use: The dark semantic mode, or high contrast
usage.why: People pick the mode they can read.

usage.use: button/focus-ring at border-width.focus, with an offset
usage.why: Focus must be seen by everyone.
Large targets help people with motor needs.
One clear next step.
Every action looks like a button people can find.

usage.use: Button secondary, then a confirm page
usage.why: A confirm step prevents a costly error.
A word says what will happen.

usage.use: The closest semantic token, then ask for a new one
usage.not: A raw value in the component
usage.why: A raw value skips the contrast checks every token passed.

usage.use: A common verb that says what happens next
usage.why: Common words are understood by the most people.

usage.use: Say what is wrong, where, and exactly how to fix it
usage.why: People must be able to fix the error without help.
usage.example: Enter your date of birth. For example, 27 3 1980.

usage.use: Confirm what happened and what comes next
usage.not: A confirmation with no next step
usage.why: People need to know the task is finished and what happens now.
usage.example: We have your application. We will email you within 5 working days.

usage.use: Explain what will appear here and how to start
usage.why: A blank page leaves people unsure if something failed.
usage.example: You have no saved applications. Start a new one below.

usage.use: Say what will happen in plain words, and offer a way back
usage.why: Plain words prevent a choice people did not mean.
usage.example: Do you want to cancel your application? Your answers will be deleted.

usage.use: Say how many steps there are and how long it takes
usage.why: Knowing the length lowers effort and anxiety.
usage.example: This takes about 10 minutes. There are 4 steps.

usage.use: a native HTML element with a label and a hint
usage.not: a custom widget that needs hover, drag or precise pointing
usage.why: Native elements work with every assistive technology without extra work.

color.$description: Colour options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

gray.$description: The gray hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

blue.$description: The blue hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

green.$description: The green hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

amber.$description: The amber hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

red.$description: The red hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

black.$description: See-through black for scrims behind dialogs, light and dark.

teal.$description: Teal ramp for the info status and categories. Same values as the multi-brand teal ramp: borrowed, not invented.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.
Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

1_2.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_25.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_3.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_4.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_5.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_6.$description: A ratio of the text size.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

fast.$description: Fast: the usual convention for feedback, about 120ms.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower, springy speed for expressive motion, about 320ms.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

default.label: Accessible first
default.description: The single brand: strong blue on true neutral, high contrast everywhere.

theme.$description: The Accessible first theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses teal, kept apart from the brand colour so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are blue, teal, green, amber, gray: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral gray.

default.$description: Height of buttons and inputs, and the smallest target.

container.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

scrim.$description: Dims the page behind a dialog.

@.$description: Info text and icons: neutral news, no action needed.

category.$description: Identity colours for tags, labels and chart series. They tell items apart and carry no meaning.

@.$description: Category 1: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 2: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 3: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 4: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 5: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.

disabled.$description: The shared look of controls that cannot be used right now.

text.$description: Text and icons of a disabled control.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring color on any button.

icon-size.$description: Size of an icon inside a button.

border.$description: Border of a disabled secondary button.

checked.$description: Fill of a checked checkbox or an on switch.

background.$description: Fill of a dialog, menu or toast.

scrim.$description: Color that dims the page behind a dialog.

content.$description: Voice tokens: the words components use for common actions. Text, not CSS.

commit.$description: The label of the action that completes a task.

cancel.$description: The label of the way out next to the main action.

destroy.$description: The label of an action that deletes data.

retry.$description: The label that repeats a failed action.

empty-action.$description: The label of the action in an empty state.
